requirements.evidence: All functional requirements and the contract are present: Queue::DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP/defaultPrefixFor (app/Models/Queue.php:24-42) and prefixForPriority (app/Models/Queue.php:49-58); validatePrefixMap enforces canonical non-negative keys, single A-Z values and effective uniqueness including the 0/10/20 fallbacks (app/Models/Queue.php:71-105); Ticket::nextCode is scoped by prefix and issue_date, ordered by id, skips malformed codes and returns prefix+'001'/last+1 (app/Models/Ticket.php:48-73); the ticket migration adds nullable issue_date, backfills DATE(issued_at), then makes it NOT NULL and swaps the unique index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_035327_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:19-39); IssueTicket reads now() once for code day, issued_at and issue_date (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:42-57); UpdateQueue has the new parameter, null/[] semantics and ValidationException mapping (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:18-42); factory alignment in database/factories/TicketFactory.php:43-82; docs/CHANGELOG updated. Only gap: the provided down() at database/migrations/2026_10_29_035327_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:52-53 cannot run once codes legitimately repeat across days.

conventions.evidence: Follows most conventions: the write goes through App\Actions\UpdateQueue with Gate authorization (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:23), priority_prefix_map stays out of the model's #[Fillable] list (app/Models/Queue.php:121), migrations use the artisan stub shape with down() methods, and docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md are updated. Clear deviation: the mandatory TDD convention is ignored (no tests in change.diff), and the migration's down() at database/migrations/2026_10_29_035327_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:52-53 is not reliably reversible, contrary to the reversible-down() rule.

security.evidence: UpdateQueue authorizes with Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue) before any write (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:23); priority_prefix_map is deliberately excluded from #[Fillable] (app/Models/Queue.php:121), so it is not mass-assignable; all map input is validated (types, canonical keys, A-Z values, uniqueness) in Queue::validatePrefixMap (app/Models/Queue.php:71-105) and re-validated in the saving hook (app/Models/Queue.php:110-140). The diff changes no views, output escaping, credentials or client-trusted IDs.

tests.evidence: change.diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, app/Actions, app/Models, database/factories, database/migrations and docs; no test file is added or updated. There is therefore no coverage for default/custom prefixes, map validation failures, per-day/per-prefix sequencing, the midnight-safe clock read, factory code allocation or UpdateQueue's ValidationException, despite the project's mandatory TDD rule.

simplicity.evidence: The change reuses the model resolver (Ticket::nextCode, Queue::defaultPrefixFor) and avoids new layers, but map validation and normalization are implemented twice: app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:26-42 pre-validates/normalizes and app/Models/Queue.php:110-140 repeats the same logic on saving. TicketFactory adds defensive paths that cannot trigger (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:52-82), and prefixForPriority has a redundant string-key branch (app/Models/Queue.php:53-55).

readability.evidence: Names and docblocks are clear and sibling style is matched, but Queue::booted holds a ~30-line validation/normalization closure (app/Models/Queue.php:110-140), TicketFactory::afterMaking mixes issue_date alignment, queue lookup and code allocation (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:43-82), and UpdateQueue's broad catch at app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php around save() relabels any InvalidArgumentException as a priority_prefix_map error.

scope.evidence: Every edit serves the task: app/Actions/IssueTicket.php, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php, app/Models/Queue.php, app/Models/Ticket.php, the two factories, the two migrations, docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md. No unrelated refactors, UI/totem/API changes or out-of-scope features are present.

issues.location: change.diff (no tests/ files in the entire diff)
issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, so none of the new prefix resolution, map validation, per-day sequencing, issuance clock, factory or UpdateQueue behavior is verified, violating the mandatory TDD convention.

down() re-adds the old unique index (queue_id, code) before dropping issue_date; as soon as the same code is issued on two different days (the new normal) the rollback fails with a duplicate-key error, so the migration is not practically reversible.

The map is validated and normalized in both UpdateQueue and the model's saving hook; the action-level validation duplicates the model's own check and creates two copies of the same rules that can drift apart.
afterMaking wraps Carbon::parse in a blanket catch (\Throwable) and checks ! is_numeric($queueId) although queue_id is typed int|null, adding defensive branches that cannot be reached.
prefixForPriority checks both int and string keys, but the array cast plus PHP's numeric-key normalization means the stored keys are always ints, so the string-key branch is dead code.
The catch around $queue->save() turns any InvalidArgumentException raised during the save into a priority_prefix_map validation error, which could misattribute an unrelated model failure.

review.summary: The change implements priority-based, daily-restarting ticket codes end to end: default and per-queue prefix resolution with model-level validation, a new tickets.issue_date column with backfill and a per-day/per-prefix unique index, clock-consistent issuance, factory alignment, and updated docs/CHANGELOG. The implementation reads correctly and meets the contract, but it ships with zero tests, which breaks the project's mandatory TDD convention, and the issue_date down() cannot be rolled back once codes repeat across days. Overall it needs tests (and a safer rollback) before merging.
